source.place: Tag 0545, lemma-help-with-powers, evaluated in an arbitrary commutative ring

proof.text: Choose $a=np^n+mp^m+n+m$ and put $P=p^a$, $B_0=np^n+mp^m$. Since $n,m>0$, $a>0$ and $a\geq n,m$. The unital subring contains natural-number casts, and $p^a(x+y)=p^{a-n}(p^nx)+p^{a-m}(p^my)$ belongs to $A$ by closure under products and sums.

source.place: Tag 0545, lemma-help-with-powers, binomial expansion and coefficient divisibility in the proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion] with exponent $P$. For each $0\leq i\leq P$, put $j=P-i$, $r=i\bmod p^n$, $s=j\bmod p^m$, and $D=nr+ms$. The remainder bounds give $D\leq B_0$, hence $D+n\leq a$ and $D+m\leq a$. It suffices to prove that $p^D$ divides $\binom Pi$ and then show each term belongs to the subring.

source.place: Tag 0545, lemma-help-with-powers, binomial expansion and coefficient divisibility in the proof

proof.text: If $r=s=0$ then $D=0$ and divisibility is immediate. If $r\ne0$, then $i>0$. Since $p^{v_p(i)}$ divides $i$ but $p^n$ does not divide $i$, we have $v_p(i)<n$. Specialize [lem-pur-prime-power-binomial-divisibility] (Mathlib WittVector.map_frobeniusPoly.key₁) at $a$ and $i-1$. It gives $p^{a-v_p(i)}\mid\binom Pi$. Since $D+n\leq a$, $D\leq a-v_p(i)$, so $p^D\mid\binom Pi$. If $r=0$ and $s\ne0$, apply the same argument with $j$ and $m$, and use $\binom Pj=\binom Pi$. The zero index is excluded by the nonzero remainder, so the argument never uses a valuation at zero.

source.place: Tag 0545, lemma-help-with-powers, binomial expansion and coefficient divisibility in the proof

proof.text: For any $q,c,x,i$, if $x^q$ and $cx$ belong to $A$, the identity $c^{i\bmod q}x^i=(x^q)^{i/q}(cx)^{i\bmod q}$ proves membership by closure under powers and products; this is the proved private helper pow_mod_mul_mem. Apply it to $(q,c,x)=(p^n,p^n,x)$ and $(p^m,p^m,y)$. Write $\binom Pi=p^D c_i$ with $c_i\in\mathbf N$ using step 3. Then the binomial term $x^iy^j\binom Pi$ is the product of $p^{nr}x^i$, $p^{ms}y^j$, and the natural-number cast $c_i$, all in $A$. Closure under finite sums gives $(x+y)^{p^a}\in A$. Combine this with step 1, with no division or cancellation in $C$.

title: Addition preserves prime-power and prime-multiple subring membership
statement: Let $p$ be a prime integer, $C$ a commutative ring, and $A\subseteq C$ a unital subring (a subset containing $1$ and closed under addition, multiplication, and additive inverses). Let $x,y\in C$ and let $n,m>0$ be integers with $x^{p^n},p^nx,y^{p^m},p^my\in A$. Then there exists an integer $a>0$ such that $(x+y)^{p^a},p^a(x+y)\in A$. Here integer multiples use the canonical $\mathbf Z$-algebra structure on $C$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], sending an integer $k$ to $k\cdot1_C$.
